name: Chapter 11: Introduction to Three Dimensional Geometry
description: Coordinate axes and planes, octants, coordinates of a point, distance formula, section formula and centroid in space.

cards.term: Why do we need three coordinates to locate a point in space?
cards.definition:
A point in space needs its distances from three mutually perpendicular planes
(like the floor and two walls of a room): x, y, z

cards.term: Coordinate axes and coordinate planes in 3-D?
cards.definition:
Axes: three mutually perpendicular lines X′OX, Y′OY, Z′OZ meeting at the origin O
Coordinate planes: the planes XY, YZ, ZX they determine

cards.term: How many octants? What are they?
cards.definition: 8: the three coordinate planes divide space into eight parts. Numbered I to VIII

cards.term: Signs of coordinates in the eight octants

cards.term: Mnemonic for the octants?
cards.definition:
Octants I–IV are above the XY-plane (z > 0), in the plane quadrant order I, II, III, IV
Octants V–VIII are the same four quadrants below the plane (z < 0)

cards.term: Example 2: octants of (−3, 1, 2) and (−3, 1, −2).

Points on the axes and planes: general forms?
cards.definition:
x-axis (x, 0, 0)
y-axis (0, y, 0)
z-axis (0, 0, z)
XY-plane (x, y, 0)
YZ-plane (0, y, z)
ZX-plane (x, 0, z)

cards.term: Ex 11.1 Q4: fill in: the x- and y-axes determine the ____; points in the XY-plane are of the form ____; the coordinate planes divide space into ____ octants.
What do x, y, z of a point P represent?
cards.definition: The perpendicular distances from the YZ, ZX and XY planes (with sign)

cards.term: Locating a point in 3-D: the coordinate box
cards.definition: P(x,y,z): x,y,z are distances from YZ, ZX, XY planes; drop a perpendicular to XY-plane at M(x,y,0) then go z up; P(3,4,2) lies in octant I

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Coordinates in space

Locate P(3, 4, 2). Which foot points does the box create, and what are the octant and distances from the planes?

Build the box from the origin.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Coordinates in space

Locate P(3, 4, 2). Which foot points does the box create, and what are the octant and distances from the planes?

Go 3 along the x-axis, 4 parallel to the y-axis (reaching M in the XY-plane), then 2 up: P(3, 4, 2) in octant I.

Distances: from the YZ-plane = |x| = 3, ZX-plane = |y| = 4, XY-plane = |z| = 2. Foot on the XY-plane is (3, 4, 0); on the x-axis (3, 0, 0).

cards.term: Example 1: P is (2, 4, 5); F is the foot on the ZX-plane? Find F.
cards.definition: F has zero distance along OY: (2, 0, 5)

cards.term: Distance of P(x, y, z) from the three axes and the three planes?
cards.definition: From the x-axis √(y² + z²), y-axis √(x² + z²), z-axis √(x² + y²); from the YZ, ZX, XY planes |x|, |y|, |z|

cards.term: Reflection of (x, y, z) in the XY-plane, in the x-axis, in the origin?
cards.definition: XY-plane: (x, y, −z) x-axis: (x, −y, −z) origin: (−x, −y, −z)

cards.term: Foot of the perpendicular from (x, y, z) to the XY-plane, to the x-axis?
Distance between P(x₁, y₁, z₁) and Q(x₂, y₂, z₂)?
Distance of Q(x, y, z) from the origin?
Distance in space as a cuboid diagonal
cards.definition: PQ = √((x2−x1)²+(y2−y1)²+(z2−z1)²): floor diagonal then Pythagoras again; origin to (2,3,6) is 7

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Distance formula in 3-D

Find the distance from the origin to Q(2, 3, 6). Explain with a box.

Do Pythagoras twice.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Distance formula in 3-D

Find the distance from the origin to Q(2, 3, 6). Explain with a box.

Floor diagonal: √(2² + 3²) = √13. Then the vertical side 6: OQ² = (√13)² + 6² = 13 + 36 = 49 ⇒ OQ = 7.

Two Pythagoras steps give PQ = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)² + (z₂ − z₁)²), the space diagonal of the cuboid on PQ.

cards.term: Example 3: distance between P(1, −3, 4) and Q(−4, 1, 2).
Example 4: show P(−2, 3, 5), Q(1, 2, 3), R(7, 0, −1) are collinear.
cards.definition: PQ = √14, QR = √56 = 2√14, PR = √126 = 3√14: PQ + QR = PR → collinear

cards.term: Method: three points collinear in space?
cards.definition:
Check that the largest distance equals the sum of the other two
(or that the direction ratios are proportional)

cards.term: Example 5: are A(3,6,9), B(10,20,30), C(25,−41,5) vertices of a right triangle?
cards.definition: AB² = 686, BC² = 4571, CA² = 2709. No pair adds to the third (686 + 2709 = 3395 ≠ 4571): not a right triangle

cards.term: Example 6: locus of P with PA² + PB² = 2k², A(3,4,5), B(−1,3,−7).

cards.definition: AB = CD = 6 and BC = DA = √43: opposite sides equal → parallelogram

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q4: the set of points equidistant from (1, 2, 3) and (3, 2, −1).
cards.definition:
Equate squared distances: −2x − 6z + 10 = −6x + 2z + 10 → x − 2z = 0
It is a plane: the perpendicular bisector plane

cards.term: Ex 11.2 Q5: points P with PA + PB = 10, A(4,0,0), B(−4,0,0).
cards.definition: A surface of revolution of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 about the x-axis:\[9x^{2} + 25y^{2} + 25z^{2} = 225\]

cards.term: Example 7: A(1,2,3), B(−1,−2,−1), C(2,3,2), D(4,7,6): parallelogram but not a rectangle?
cards.definition: AB = CD = 6 and BC = DA = √43 → parallelogram. Diagonals AC = √3 and BD = √155 are unequal → not a rectangle

cards.term: Example 8: equidistant from A(3,4,−5) and B(−2,1,4).
Method: the set of points equidistant from two points.
cards.definition:
Square PA = PB and expand.
The squares cancel and you get a linear equation: a plane
(the perpendicular bisector plane of AB)

cards.term: Locus with PA² + PB² = constant: shape?
cards.definition: A sphere centred at the midpoint of AB (x², y², z² all appear with the same coefficient)

cards.term: Beyond the textbook text (Class 12 and JEE): section formula for P dividing AB internally in the ratio m : n?
cards.definition: \[\left(\dfrac{mx_2 + nx_1}{m+n},\ \dfrac{my_2 + ny_1}{m+n},\ \dfrac{mz_2 + nz_1}{m+n}\right)\](external: replace n by −n)

cards.term: Midpoint and centroid formulas in space?
cards.definition: Midpoint ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2, (z₁ + z₂)/2) centroid of a triangle ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃)/3, …) of a tetrahedron divide by 4

cards.term: Example 9: centroid (1, 1, 1), A(3, −5, 7), B(−1, 7, −6). Find C.
Misc Q1: parallelogram ABCD with A(3, −1, 2), B(1, 2, −4), C(−1, 1, 2). Find D.
cards.definition: Diagonals bisect: D = A + C − B = (1, −2, 8)

cards.term: Misc Q2: lengths of the medians of the triangle A(0,0,6), B(0,4,0), C(6,0,0).
Misc Q3: origin is the centroid of P(2a, 2, 6), Q(−4, 3b, −10), R(8, 14, 2c). Find a, b, c.
Equation of a sphere with centre (a, b, c) and radius r?
cards.definition: (x − a)² + (y − b)² + (z − c)² = r²; x² + y² + z² = r² for a sphere at the origin

cards.term: Length of the diagonal of a cuboid with edges l, b, h?
cards.definition: \[\sqrt{l^2 + b^2 + h^2}\]Cube of side a: a√3
